changes.summary: In 1946, Max Ernst and Dorothea Tanning left New York City, then the center of the Euro-American art world, for Sedona, Arizona. Over the next ten years, they created some of the most significant works of their careers in this small desert town. Sedona Surreal will reunite the paintings, sculptures, and other artworks that they made there, exploring the construction of artistic modernism far from a large urban center. It will be the first museum exhibition devoted to Ernst and Tanning’s pivotal time in the Southwest. Why do artists remain in cities? Must they chum with collectors, attend openings, witness name-droppings in upper east and west side pastures...in order to make good pictures, good objects, and good anything? No, we will do it the other way. Sedona Surreal: Max Ernst and Dorothea Tanning in the American Southwest is curated by Natalie Dupêcher, Associate Curator of Modern Art, The Menil Collection.
